prompt: Trina has decided to use a ternary counting system (base $3$). If she read the expression of $2020$ in ternary as a date, how many days from today would it be? (Today is February 22, 2020.)

solutions.title: Convert and count days
solutions.body:
In base $3$, $2020=2\cdot3^6+2\cdot3^5+0\cdot3^4+\dots$; explicitly $2020_{10}=2202211_3$. Read as a date this is $2/20/2211$ (February 20, 2211).

From February 22, 2020 to February 22, 2211 there are $191$ years, i.e. $191\cdot365$ days plus the leap days in between. The leap days (Feb 29) occurring after Feb 22, 2020 and up to Feb 2211 are those of the years $2020,2024,\dots,2208$ ($48$ years) minus the years $2100$ and $2200$, which are not leap years: $46$. So February 22, 2211 is $191\cdot365+46=69761$ days later, and February 20, 2211 is $2$ days earlier: $69761-2=69759$ days.

**Answer: 69759**

reviewNote: Depends on the contest date (February 22, 2020) and on reading 2202211 as 2/20/2211. The official key says 69760 because it counts 47 leap days; 2200 is not a leap year, so the correct count is 69759.

prompt: A pen is tethered to the corner of a square box of side length $2$ cm by a string of length $4$ cm. What is the area of the largest shape that can be drawn with the pen without breaking the string and without the string going through the box? (Do not count the area of the box.)

solutions.title: Add the circular sectors
solutions.body:
With the string anchored at corner $P$, the pen can sweep a $270^\circ$ sector of radius $4$ outside the box: area $\frac34\pi\cdot16=12\pi$. Once the string wraps around an adjacent corner ($2$ cm along a side), the remaining length is $2$ cm and the pen sweeps a quarter circle of radius $2$ around each of the two adjacent corners: $2\cdot\frac14\pi\cdot4=2\pi$. The two quarter circles stop exactly at the opposite corner (the string is then fully wrapped). Total: $12\pi+2\pi=14\pi$ cm$^2$.

**Answer: $14\pi$**

prompt: Suppose $S$ is a set of functions with the property that, if $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are in $S$, then $(f\circ g)(x)=f(g(x))$ is in $S$. Given that the functions $r(x)=\dfrac{x\sqrt3+1}{\sqrt3-x}$ and $s(x)=\dfrac1x$ are in $S$, compute the smallest possible size of $S$.
